messages:
maria: quick proposal — lease-orchestrator daemon to coordinate prefetches during deploys/scale-outs. avoids redundant full-warmer runs and smooths GPU usage.
jon: high level pls :+1: what's the lease model?
maria: single coordinator per GPU pool. it issues short 'leases' to workers. a lease = list of prefix samples, target shard ids, timebox, and priority flag.
kevin: how do workers pick actual KV keys? coordinator precomputes hashes or workers compute locally?
maria: workers compute per-prefix KV keys to respect local sharding and runtime-version namespace. coordinator only ships metadata.
anu: what about long-tail prefixes? sampling bias could leave cold tails.
maria: mix top-live prefixes + synthetic tail samples. rotate tail coverage across deploys to eventually hit long-tail.
sasha: any smoke perf from a run?
warmup-bot: smoke 2026-02-14-cascade-vs-naive
warmup-bot: naive-full-warmer (baseline)
  - post-deploy KV hit-rate: 18.7%
  - p50 cold-tail latency: 430ms
  - extra GPU-minutes per deploy: 101m
warmup-bot: lease-orch-run-1
  - post-deploy KV hit-rate: 56.9% (+38.2pp)
  - p50 cold-tail latency: 308ms (-28%)
  - extra GPU-minutes per deploy: 27m (-73%)
kevin: solid drop in GPU minutes. what's the sampling universe and hardware?
maria: 10k live prefixes sampled from top routes, ran across a prod-like g5x2 cluster, mix skewed to short prompts (mean 64 tokens). included 10% synthetic tail in every lease.
jon: how do we handle overlapping deploys (canary then main)?
maria: coordinator keeps deploy lineage id + seq. later deploys can preempt leases (TTL-based) so handoffs are graceful.
anu: autoscaler events are noisy. do we warm on every scale out?
maria: autoscaler -> event batching window (30s). within window coordinator issues low-priority leases. for large scale-outs switch to 'bulk-mode' and only warm hottest prefixes.
kevin: how to pick hottest prefixes in bulk-mode?
maria: heuristic = top-N by recent token volume + bloom checks to avoid expired keys. limit per-batch to keep token throughput under QoS threshold.
sasha: multi-tenant pools risk warming other tenants' shard keys.
maria: coordinator issues tenant-scoped leases; workers validate tenant ACLs before prefetch and drop any cross-tenant keys.
jon: need audit + telemetry for prefetch ops.
maria: add prefetch traces and counts to console; will emit per-lease telemetry (prefix_count, prefetch_success, errors).
anu: config example pls
maria: sure
```
coordinator:
  lease_ttl_s: 45
  max_concurrent_leases: 8
  sample_budget_per_lease: 120
  tail_fraction: 0.10
  prefetch_token_window: [0, 128]
  bulk_mode_threshold_gpus: 12
  batch_window_s: 30
  precompute_hashes: false
```
kevin: rollout plan?
maria: phased rollout:
  1) canary on low-traffic pool (2w). gates: post-deploy hit-rate >= baseline +10pp AND extra GPU-minutes <= baseline * 0.5
  2) beta on capacity pool (monitor tail error rate 1w)
  3) gradual global
jon: add kill-switch + automatic backoff if backend latency climbs or if hit-rate drops unexpectedly.
maria: will add throttling/backoff state to coordinator and playbook alerts for eng-sre.
anu: i'll build an eval suite focusing on long-tail prefixes, cross-tenant collision cases, and version-namespace contamination.
sasha: i'll add SDK hooks and docs for teams to opt-in per-pool. also add prometheus queries for per-lease metrics.
warmup-bot: artifacts: s3://redwood-experiments/lease-orch/2026-02-14/ (promql, raw-histograms, traces)
jon: action items
- maria: push coordinator alpha + canary config
- kevin: tenant scoping + prefetch telemetry
- sasha: docs + SDK hooks PR
- anu: canary eval suite
- jon: alerting/playbook
maria: thanks team :rocket: starting canary next Tue, will post status to #eng-runtime when it goes live
